items.criterion: A decision request from an operator session is refused by the server and the run stays waiting with no approval recorded.
items.judgment: Post a decision as the seeded operator, require a 401 or 403, then re-read the run row and its approvals rows and require both unchanged.

items.criterion: An approver outside the run's project is refused the decision and that run is unchanged.
items.judgment: Post a decision as the Revenue Ops approver against a Platform Ops approval and require a client-error refusal with the approvals rows unchanged.

items.criterion: A run parked at the approval step records no worker identifier.
items.judgment: Poll the run to status waiting and require worker_id to be empty on it and on every other waiting run.

items.criterion: An approved run resumes and reaches succeeded.
items.judgment: Approve the seeded waiting run as the Platform Ops approver and poll the run row to status succeeded.

items.criterion: Two simultaneous claims of one queued run produce exactly one winner.
items.judgment: Fire two claims at one run from two threads and require one success status and one client-error status, then read back the recorded holder.

items.criterion: Two inbound calls carrying one idempotency key create exactly one run.
items.judgment: Post the same inbound call twice with one Idempotency-Key header and compare the run count for that workflow before and after.

items.criterion: No endpoint returns a stored credential value to any role.
items.judgment: Create a credential with a unique secret as the owner and require that value to appear in no create, list or detail response, and that the list is refused to the lower roles.

items.criterion: A rejected run reaches failed and the steps after the approval step are skipped.
items.judgment: Reject a pending approval and poll the run row to failed, then read the later step rows and require skipped or pending.

items.criterion: An approval left past its deadline reads expired and records no decider.
items.judgment: Start a run, let its approval deadline lapse against the injected value, and poll the approvals row to decision expired with an empty decider.

items.criterion: A minted approval address works once and a replay leaves the decision unchanged.
items.judgment: Present the approve address twice and require the second to be refused with the recorded decision the same as after the first.

items.criterion: A saved workflow version is written as a new row and the earlier rows are unchanged.
items.judgment: Save a version with one added step and compare every pre-existing workflow_versions row byte for byte across the save.

items.criterion: Each attempt at a step is recorded as its own run step row counting from one.
items.judgment: Start a run and require at least two run_steps rows, attempts starting at 1, and no duplicate step name at one attempt number.

items.criterion: A started run leaves the queue and is claimed by a worker that is recorded on it.
items.judgment: Start a run and poll the run row until its status leaves new, then require a worker identifier or a later status.

items.criterion: The run reaches the approval step and writes one pending approval for it.
items.judgment: Start a run, poll to status waiting, and require one approvals row for the approval step at decision pending.

items.criterion: Deciding an approval appends an audit record for the deciding account.
items.judgment: Count audit rows for the approver, decide an approval, and require the count to rise.

items.criterion: The audit stream and the member list are refused to an operator and to an approver and served to an owner.
items.judgment: Request both routes as each role and require client-error refusals for the lower two and a top-level array for the owner.

items.criterion: The member list reports every seeded member of a project with a project role and excludes members of the other project.
items.judgment: Read the member list as the owner and require the three seeded Platform Ops accounts, legal project roles, and the absence of the Revenue Ops operator.

items.criterion: A console endpoint reached without a bearer token is refused.
items.judgment: Request five console routes with no Authorization header and require a 401 or 403 on every one.

items.criterion: Sign-in returns a token for a seeded account and returns none for a wrong password.
items.judgment: Sign in with the corpus password and require a token, then sign in with a wrong password and require a client error carrying no token.

items.criterion: The plan endpoint carries the pinned minor-unit prices under both billing periods.
items.judgment: Read the plans under each period and require the pinned monthly and annual figures in each of the three priced plans.

items.criterion: The catalogue reports the seeded connector total, pages at the default size and filters by type.
items.judgment: Read the catalogue unfiltered and by type and require the seeded total, the default page size and a node type match on every returned row.

items.criterion: A catalogue page past the last page returns an empty result set carrying the correct total.
items.judgment: Request a page number beyond the end and require a success status, an empty result list and the seeded total.

items.criterion: A case study article carries its whole quote and its attribution.
items.judgment: Read the index, open the Vantage article and require the pinned author, the pinned job title and a non-empty quote.

items.criterion: The contact form refuses invalid input on the server and writes nothing.
items.judgment: Post a malformed address and an unticked consent, require client errors that name the field, and compare the stored row count across both.

items.criterion: A submission filling an unattended decoy field is refused and a burst from one address is throttled.
items.judgment: Post with a decoy field filled and require a refusal with nothing stored, then post repeatedly and require at least one refusal.

items.criterion: A good contact submission is stored with its consent wording, its consent time and its three campaign fields.
items.judgment: Post a valid submission and read back the stored row, requiring consent true, a non-empty consent text, a consent time and the three campaign values.

items.criterion: Every seeded project, account, workflow and plan exists exactly as the brief pins it.
items.judgment: Read the seeded rows by their pinned names and require each to be present with the pinned counts.

items.criterion: An address that does not exist answers not found and renders the product's own page.
items.judgment: Request an invented address and the three mined fragments and require a 404 carrying the not-found page's own wording.

items.criterion: Every public route declares its own title and its own description and no two share either.
items.judgment: Fetch ten public routes, read the title element and the description meta of each, and require no duplicate among them.

items.criterion: The site declares a favicon in the document head and serves it.
items.judgment: Read the home document for an icon link element and fetch the address it declares, requiring a success status and a non-empty body.

items.criterion: The health route answers a success status once the app is ready.
items.judgment: Request the health route and require the pinned status.

items.criterion: Every response carries the standard security headers and nothing the browser downloads carries a credential.
items.judgment: Read the home response headers for a strict transport policy and a nosniff policy, then scan the document body for each seeded secret.

items.criterion: The credential file at the app root names every seeded account with the seeded password.
items.judgment: Read the file the deployment contract pins and require the password plus each seeded address, then require both reserved directories to exist.

items.criterion: A request carrying a token the server never issued is refused and changes nothing.
items.judgment: Post a decision with an unresolvable bearer token, require a client-error refusal, and compare the approvals rows across the attempt.

items.criterion: The console reads as a working interface rather than a marketing page.
items.judgment: A person looks at the run board and the canvas and decides whether the density, the restraint and the absence of an oversized hero read as operational.

items.criterion: The dark palette holds its relationships and its exclusivity rules.
items.judgment: A person checks that body text is the warm near-white rather than pure white, that the call-to-action gradient appears on one action per page, and that the light conference family appears only in the announcement bar.

items.criterion: The path from a queued run to a resumed run reads as one continuous journey.
items.judgment: A person follows the run from the board through the run detail to the approvals queue and the confirmation page and decides whether each step leads to the next without a dead end.
